display.purpose: Page H1 only, one per page. Five per-page clamps share a 34px mobile floor and differ only at the desktop ceiling.

headline.purpose: Every H2 site-wide. Legal pages take a lower ceiling but the same 24px floor.

title.purpose: H3 - card headings, service group headings, legal sub-points.

deck.purpose: The serif paragraph directly under an H1. A supporting voice, never a second heading.

quote.purpose: Pull quotes only. The system's only italic.

stat.purpose: Numbers band figures. Units inside a figure drop to 28px at weight 500.

body.purpose: Running text. Measure set per block in ch (20-68), never left to fill the container.

label.purpose: Tracked uppercase for eyebrows, tags, column heads, and field labels. Never a heading level; always nowrap.

motion.name: transition-base
motion.purpose: The only transition in the system. Applies to color, background, and border-color on hover and focus - never to transform, opacity, or shadow.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Global prefers-reduced-motion override; also disables smooth scrolling.

geometry.name: radius
geometry.purpose: Every corner in the system. Not a knob to turn.

geometry.name: rule-hairline
geometry.purpose: Dividers: sections, dl rows, service rows, card borders.

geometry.name: rule-brand
geometry.purpose: The gold brand rule on interior pages, and the active nav underline.

geometry.name: rule-heavy
geometry.purpose: Pull-quote bind, CONFIRM callout border, hero top and bottom edges.

geometry.name: focus-ring
geometry.purpose: Every interactive element. An accessibility requirement, not styling.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The site's main call to action. Navy fill, square, darkens on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn { display: inline-block; border-radius: 0; border: 1px solid transparent; font-family: Archivo, system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.3px; white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; text-align: center; transition: background 180ms ease, border-color 180ms ease, color 180ms ease; } .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--nta-navy, #16324d); border-color: var(--nta-navy, #16324d); color: #fff; padding: 17px 34px; font-size: 19px; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: var(--nta-navy-hover, #0f2437); border-color: var(--nta-navy-hover, #0f2437); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--nta-slate, #2c5f8a); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: On-Navy Button
components.description: For the navy hero. White fill inverting to gold on hover - the one place gold fills an area.
components.css: .ds-navy-stage { background: var(--nta-navy, #16324d); padding: 32px; } .ds-btn-on-navy { background: #fff; border-color: #fff; color: var(--nta-navy, #16324d); padding: 17px 34px; font-size: 19px; } .ds-btn-on-navy:hover { background: var(--nta-gold, #c9a24a); border-color: var(--nta-gold, #c9a24a); color: var(--nta-navy, #16324d); } .ds-btn-on-navy:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #fff; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: Secondary action, such as the contact form's reset. Fills navy on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { background: transparent; border-color: var(--nta-navy, #16324d); color: var(--nta-navy, #16324d); padding: 13px 26px; font-size: 16px; } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: var(--nta-navy, #16324d); color: #fff; } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--nta-slate, #2c5f8a); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Tracked uppercase label stacked above a square field with a cool hairline border.
components.css: .ds-field { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 8px; max-width: 360px; } .ds-field__label { font-family: Archivo, system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 3px; white-space: nowrap; color: var(--nta-navy, #16324d); } .ds-field__input { border: 1px solid var(--nta-line-cool, #e2e5e9); border-radius: 0; padding: 14px; font-family: Archivo, system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.6; color: var(--nta-body, #3c4652); background: #fff; outline: none; transition: border-color 180ms ease; } .ds-field__input::placeholder { color: var(--nta-muted-light, #b3b8bf); opacity: 1; } .ds-field__input:focus { border-color: var(--nta-slate, #2c5f8a); } .ds-field__input:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--nta-slate, #2c5f8a); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Paper Card
components.description: Paper ground on a white section, 1px warm hairline, no shadow. The ground always inverts against its section.

narrative.overview:
The system is built on a double meaning that belongs only to this practice. The corner ticks framing the hero and the headshot are printer's registration marks — the crosshairs that prove a sheet was pulled in alignment. Registration is also what a Series 27 is. The mark itself is a ledger cell with those ticks set into it, so the identity's smallest element already carries both readings: a page pulled correctly, and a professional on the register.

Everything follows from treating the surface as a printed sheet rather than a screen. Paper (#faf8f3) and white are the two grounds, separated by tone and a 1px warm hairline rather than by shadow. Corners are square because a trimmed sheet has square corners. Gold appears the way a press mark appears — as trim at the edge of the work, never as a field, and never carrying body copy. Spectral sets the display type with the weight of a set page; Archivo handles everything a form or a label needs. Depth is entirely tonal; there is no elevation ramp, because a sheet does not float.

The restraint is doing strategic work, not just aesthetic work. This practice's differentiator is that one person handles both a broker-dealer's net capital computation and a family's late return, without changing voice between them. A system that performed for either audience would break that. So the design proves competence by refusing to perform it: correct alignment, exact hairlines, credentials stated as dates and numbers, and no ornament anywhere that a compliance reviewer would have to look past.
keyCharacteristics: Flat by construction — no shadows, no gradients, no radius anywhere.
Two grounds only: white and paper, divided by 1px warm hairlines.
Gold is trim, strictly rationed to two sanctioned rule placements plus the tick pairs.
Serif display against sans UI; tracked uppercase is always a label, never a heading.
Type scales by clamp() from a 390px reference, so layout breakpoints stay layout-only.
Registration ticks appear in diagonal pairs, never four corners.

rules.name: The Deep Gold Rule
rules.body: Registration Gold is never type on a light field — it measures 2.3:1 and fails AA. When gold must be typographic on white or paper, it is Deep Gold (4.6:1). There is no exception, including for large display sizes.

rules.name: The Trim Rule
rules.body: Gold marks edges; it does not fill areas. Ticks, rules, a 2px active underline, a 3px callout border. The single exception is the on-navy button's hover fill, where gold sits against navy rather than paper.

rules.name: The Real Heading Rule
rules.body: Tracked uppercase is a label, never a heading level. If a line is an H2 or H3, it gets real serif type at real heading size. Caps treatment marks an eyebrow, tag, column head, or field label — nothing else.

rules.name: The No-Wrap Rule
rules.body: Every tracked uppercase label carries white-space: nowrap. The tracking consumes the last pixel of the line box, so a label silently re-breaks on a font fallback. A label that will not fit at 390px gets shorter copy — the label__long / label__short pair — never a wrap.

rules.name: The One Size Per Level Rule
rules.body: At the 390px reference, every H1 is 34px, every H2 is 24px, every H3 is 22px — across marketing and legal pages alike. Clamp ceilings differ; the mobile floor does not. Four sizes doing the work of two heading levels is the failure this rule prevents.

rules.name: The Clamp-Not-Breakpoint Rule
rules.body: Type scales by clamp() from the 390px reference to the desktop comp value, and letter-spacing is expressed in em so it tracks the clamp. The breakpoints that exist (900px, 620px, 860px for the header) are layout-only. Adding a type media query means the clamp was wrong.

rules.name: The Flat Rule
rules.body: A box-shadow, gradient, blur, or transform-on-hover anywhere in this system is a bug, not an enhancement. Surfaces separate by tone and hairline. An earlier offset-block button treatment was explicitly rejected during design — do not reintroduce drop-shadow or offset effects under any name.

rules.name: The Square Corner Rule
rules.body: Radius is 0 everywhere. Not softened for cards, not softened for inputs, not softened for images, not softened just for the mobile menu.

rules.name: The Two Sanctioned Gold Rules
rules.body: Gold rules have exactly two placements. (1) Page opener — one horizontal rule under a page's own H1, 160x4px on the home hero and 88x2px on interior pages. (2) Vertical bind — a 2-3px vertical rule joining two things that belong together: the mark to the wordmark in the lockup, and a pull quote to its attribution. A third placement is a bug, not a new pattern.

rules.name: The Diagonal Tick Rule
rules.body: Ticks are always a top-right / bottom-left pair. Four corners reads as a border and destroys the registration-mark meaning; two reads as alignment. They also degrade — below 32px the mark drops its ticks entirely rather than shipping them clipped.

dos: Do use Deep Gold (#8a6a1e) whenever gold must be typographic on a light ground; Registration Gold is trim only.
Do invert the card's ground against its section — paper card on white, white card on paper. That inversion is the entire elevation system.
Do give a tracked uppercase label white-space: nowrap, and shorten its copy rather than let it wrap at 390px.
Do hold one size per heading level at the 390px reference: H1 34px, H2 24px, H3 22px, on every page type.
Do scale type with clamp() from the mobile reference and express letter-spacing in em so it tracks.
Do set line measure per block with the ch helpers rather than letting text fill the container.
Do render the logo from the locked brand-asset files in public/assets/ — mark SVGs for header/legal-header, the full lockup PNG for the footer. Never rebuild it from live text/CSS.
Do keep the 3px slate focus ring at 2px offset on every interactive element — it is an accessibility requirement, not styling.
donts: Don't add a box-shadow, gradient, blur, scale, or offset-block effect anywhere. The system is flat by construction, and the offset-block button was explicitly rejected once already.
Don't soften a corner. Radius is 0 for buttons, cards, inputs, panels, and images alike.
Don't place a gold rule anywhere outside the two sanctioned uses — page opener under an H1, or vertical bind between two related elements.
Don't draw ticks on four corners; the diagonal pair is what makes them registration marks rather than a frame.
Don't use tracked uppercase as a heading level, or serif display type as a label.
Don't put Registration Gold on paper or white as text, at any size or weight.
Don't add a type media query — if the type is wrong at a width, the clamp is wrong.
Don't introduce a second accent color, a cool grey into the warm hairline family, or a shadow-based card that competes with the paper/white inversion.

Don't resemble the generic small-practice accountant template (corporate blue, stock handshakes, rounded cards), fintech SaaS (gradient mesh, glassmorphism, neon dark mode), or big-four corporate polish. The last one is the sharpest rejection: faceless enterprise gloss implies a large team, which is the exact opposite of this practice's differentiator.
